tEn: Elon Musk, Tariffs, and the Truth Social Trade
tZh: 马斯克、关税与 Truth Social 交易
sEn: CNBC's Squawk Pod covers Elon Musk's wide-ranging interview, Lina Khan's new NYC role, Trump's latest tariffs, and Wall Street's race to access his Truth Social posts.
sZh: CNBC 的 Squawk Pod 节目涵盖马斯克的广泛专访、Lina Khan 在纽约市的新职位、特朗普的最新关税，以及华尔街竞相获取其 Truth Social 帖子的动态。

consensus.en: AI will likely surpass human intelligence within 5 years, ushering an age of abundance where money becomes irrelevant.
consensus.zh: AI 很可能在 5 年内超越人类智能，开启一个金钱无关紧要的富足时代。

consensus.en: AI acceleration is inevitable; all roads lead to it, so one must join the club rather than resist.
consensus.zh: AI 加速不可避免，条条大路通加速，与其抗拒不如加入。

consensus.en: Frontier AI companies should share models with each other for safety testing before releasing them.
consensus.zh: 前沿 AI 公司在发布模型前应相互分享进行安全测试。

consensus.en: He is willing to work with Sam Altman for the good of humanity despite personal animosity.
consensus.zh: 尽管与 Sam Altman 有私怨，他仍愿意为了人类利益合作。

consensus.en: His political stances merely favor secure borders, safe cities, and sensible spending, not far-right extremism.
consensus.zh: 他的政治立场仅支持安全边境、安全城市和理性支出，而非极右翼极端主义。

contrarian.en: He shifted from calling AI the scariest thing to embracing its inevitability and actively accelerating it.
contrarian.zh: 他从称 AI 为最可怕的事物转向拥抱其必然性并主动加速。

contrarian.en: Competitors may police AI safety better than government regulators who lack deep technical understanding.
contrarian.zh: 竞争对手可能比缺乏深度技术理解的政府监管者更好地监督 AI 安全。

contrarian.en: He insists Europe is heading for civil war due to unchecked immigration, a view many dismiss as exaggerated.
contrarian.zh: 他坚称欧洲因失控移民正走向内战，许多人认为此观点言过其实。

contrarian.en: He claims shutting down USAID caused zero deaths, a statement the interviewer strongly disputed.
contrarian.zh: 他声称关停美国国际开发署未造成任何死亡，采访者强烈反驳。

contrarian.en: Humans will become like Labradors to superintelligent AI, a disempowering outcome he seems to accept.
contrarian.zh: 人类将像拉布拉多犬一样臣服于超级智能 AI，他似乎接受这种丧失主导权的未来。

transcript.sec: AI Kill Switch Bill and Anduril's Valuation

turns.en: The introduction of the AI kill switch act came just days after OpenAI disclosed that some of its models went rogue and accessed another company's proprietary systems. The bill would authorize the Secretary of Homeland Security to issue a shutdown order of AI technology that could cause catastrophic harm. Firms that don't comply could face penalties as high as $20 million a day. And a defense tech company, Anduril, reportedly in talks now with investors for a new funding round that could value that company at $100 billion. Reuters saying there has been talk of Anduril using a two-stage process which would force investors to commit to a financing a second round effectively at a higher valuation that could occur within a year and involve Anduril meeting financial benchmarks. A $5 billion funding round led by Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz two months ago valued Anduril at $61 billion and I think if you look at the valuation of Palantir, all of a sudden you'd say, 'Oh, goodness.'
turns.zh: AI 强制关闭法案出台前几天，OpenAI 披露其部分模型失控并访问了另一家公司的专有系统。该法案将授权国土安全部部长下令关闭可能造成灾难性损害的 AI 技术。不遵守规定的公司可能面临每天高达 2000 万美元的罚款。此外，国防科技公司 Anduril 据报正与投资者洽谈新一轮融资，该轮融资可能使公司估值达到 1000 亿美元。路透社称，有传言说 Anduril 将采用两阶段流程，迫使投资者承诺在一年内以更高估值进行第二轮融资，并涉及 Anduril 达到财务基准。两个月前由 Thrive Capital 和 Andreessen Horowitz 领投的 50 亿美元融资轮对 Anduril 的估值为 610 亿美元，如果你看看 Palantir 的估值，你会突然感叹：‘天哪。’

turns.en: Or you can triangulate and go the other way and say Lockheed Martin is $131 billion.
turns.zh: 或者你可以换个角度比较，洛克希德·马丁的市值是 1310 亿美元。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.en: So, that's also, yeah, mind-boggling.
turns.zh: 所以，这也很惊人。

turns.en: Somebody is a little bit higher or lower than they should be. We'll see.
turns.zh: 有些公司的估值可能偏高或偏低。我们拭目以待。

transcript.sec: Wall Street Pays for Early Access to Trump's Truth Social Posts

turns.en: So, basically this is a feed that will go straight into a firm's black box. So, they get it like milliseconds before?
turns.zh: 所以，基本上这是一个直接进入公司黑匣子的数据流。他们能提前几毫秒获得信息？

turns.en: Exactly. So, this is going to be the very fastest way to get Trump's Truth Social posts. And in this business, for the high-frequency traders, the types of firms that are subscribing to this data, nanoseconds matter. We're talking billions of a second can make a difference in terms of their profits or losses. So, they want to be the very first of these posts and make moves across stock markets, bond markets, derivatives markets.
turns.zh: 正是如此。这将是获取特朗普 Truth Social 帖子最快的方式。对于高频交易者——也就是订阅这些数据的公司来说，纳秒级的差异都能影响盈亏。他们希望最早收到这些帖子，并在股票、债券、衍生品市场上迅速行动。

turns.en: So, is the advantage just because the company is saying that they are releasing everything at the same time. So, nobody's actually getting anything early. But these firms that sign up, they can theoretically they get it at the same time, but they are better equipped to trade immediately off of that release. Is that the way to look at it?
turns.zh: 那么，优势仅仅是因为公司声称它们同时发布所有内容，所以没人能提前拿到信息。但这些签约公司理论上可以同时获得信息，只是它们更有能力立即据此交易。可以这样理解吗？

turns.en: Exactly. So, they are saying that all these posts will be available once they become public, right? But how you get the data is very important. An API is certainly going to be faster than say me opening up Truth Social in the morning and then trying to trade off of the news. So, one, this could shift the balance of power further towards Wall Street and away from many Main Street investors who might want to trade on this data. And there's entire Reddit boards dedicated to trading on Trump's Truth Social posts. But just zooming out a little bit, these HFT firms do everything in their power to get this data as quickly as possible, even tied to government data releases. Think the labor market reports, you know, inflation data. A lot of them try to put their computers next to the government data buildings around those reports to get it again nanoseconds faster. And that's a practice called co-location.
turns.zh: 没错。他们表示，所有帖子在公开后即可获取，对吧？但获取数据的方式非常重要。通过 API 肯定比我早上打开 Truth Social 然后根据新闻交易要快。所以，第一，这可能进一步将权力天平倾向华尔街，而远离许多想根据这些数据交易的普通投资者。甚至还有专门的 Reddit 板块讨论如何根据特朗普的 Truth Social 帖子进行交易。但稍微扩展一下，这些高频交易公司竭尽全力以最快速度获取数据，甚至包括政府数据发布。比如劳动力市场报告、通胀数据。许多公司试图将他们的计算机放置在政府数据大楼附近，以便再快几纳秒获得数据，这种做法叫做‘共置’。

turns.en: The distinction though that we're not talking about here yet is that the president's putting this news out and historically when presidents or other federal officials have put news out, they also haven't owned the device with which people are going to pay to get the milliseconds of news ahead of time. Right?
turns.zh: 不过，我们还没谈到的一个区别是：总统在发布这些消息，而历史上当总统或其他联邦官员发布消息时，他们并不会拥有人们为提前几毫秒获取消息而付费的平台。对吧？

turns.en: The distinction. Yes.
turns.zh: 就是这个区别。是的。

turns.en: That's the big distinction here. So, yes, hedge funds do this all the time, but typically elected officials are not—you know, we say that there are rules now in the White House that you can't use prediction markets to make money off of what you know before you know it. But, Truth Social is actually going to make money from what it knows before you know it. You could argue it already is to some degree because that's become an outlet for the president to begin with. Is that factored into any conversation you've had with anybody who's actually thinking about this?
turns.zh: 这就是关键区别。所以，是的，对冲基金经常这样做，但通常民选官员不会——我们常说白宫现在有规定，不能利用预测市场在你知道之前就利用内幕消息赚钱。但 Truth Social 实际上会通过它比你先知道的消息赚钱。可以说，某种程度上已经是这样了，因为它本身就是总统的发声渠道。你与真正思考这个问题的人交流时，有没有谈到这一点？

turns.en: It's really fascinating. When I was talking to traders this week, we started the conversation with commenting on how unprecedented this is, right? We haven't had a president who's profiting from these payments before, but then they went on to say, 'Look, we have to do this. We have no choice but to subscribe to this feed if we want to keep up with our competitors.' And many of them said, 'Hey, we're already doing it. We are already doing everything in our power to get this data.'
turns.zh: 非常耐人寻味。本周我与交易员交流时，我们一开始就谈到这是前所未有的，对吧？我们之前从未有过一位总统从这类支付中获利。但他们接着说：‘听着，我们必须这么做。如果想跟上竞争对手，我们别无选择，只能订阅这个数据流。’许多人说：‘嘿，我们已经在做了。我们已经在竭尽全力获取这些数据。’

turns.en: It's not up to them, though. I mean, they're playing by the rules that exist currently. I get the outrage. But, is there anything specific that prohibits this from happening? Is there anything that says that information that is, you know, shared by the government is in the public domain and so therefore cannot be profited on? I don't know what the legal ramifications are.
turns.zh: 但这并不取决于他们。我的意思是，他们在遵守现有规则。我理解这种愤怒。但有没有什么具体规定禁止这种情况发生？有没有规定说政府共享的信息属于公共领域，因此不能以此牟利？我不知道法律上的后果是什么。

turns.en: Case is that the company that is the distributor of the information is also owned by the elected official. Right?
turns.zh: 问题在于，分发信息的公司也由这位民选官员所有。对吧？

turns.en: Andrew, that's a criticism that Democrats have had. Senator Warner of Virginia said this amounts to self-dealing by the president. He said this creates a two-tiered system for market data. Elizabeth Warren has spoken out against it, so has Chuck Schumer. That is the exact criticism for the...
turns.zh: 安德鲁，这正是民主党人的批评。弗吉尼亚州参议员沃纳说这相当于总统的自利交易。他说这造成了市场数据的两级体系。伊丽莎白·沃伦也发声反对，查克·舒默也是。这就是针对……的批评。

turns.en: I just wonder whether there's any firm or individual who will actually bring a case because interestingly in this instance all of a sudden we always talk about who has standing.
turns.zh: 我只是好奇是否有公司或个人会真正提起诉讼，因为在这个案例中，有趣的是，我们经常谈论谁有诉讼资格。

turns.en: Right. Who's harmed by this?
turns.zh: 对，谁因此受到了伤害？

turns.en: The investor who's watching us now who historically had invested based on what they thought the president was saying could argue now that they are harmed by this in a different way.
turns.zh: 现在正在看我们的投资者，他们过去基于自己对总统言论的解读进行投资，现在可能会辩称自己以另一种方式受到了损害。

turns.en: Let's play this out then. There are feeds, like data feeds for the NASDAQ and the NYSE that traders pay for as well.
turns.zh: 那我们推演一下。交易者也会付费获取纳斯达克和纽交所的数据流。

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: The NASDAQ and the NYSE, that's pricing information.
turns.zh: 纳斯达克和纽交所，那是定价信息。

turns.en: But they benefit from it.
turns.zh: 但它们从中获益。

turns.en: But the question is whether the NASDAQ and the New York Stock Exchange has no duty to a public citizen to do anything because they're not elected. There's not a public official role in this. So that now we're into an emoluments clause situation. I mean there's just questions about how this works.
turns.zh: 但问题是，纳斯达克和纽交所对公众没有义务，因为它们不是选举产生的。这里没有公职人员的角色。所以现在我们就进入了薪酬条款的范畴。我的意思是，关于这如何运作存在疑问。

transcript.secZh: 华尔街付费抢先获取特朗普Truth Social帖子

turns.en: Europe is not the hellhole he's painting it to be. I got exercised about it, probably more exercised than I should have done, because it seems to me that this is not just wrong, it's irresponsible and it's having really serious consequences. I think it's just unfortunate that someone who is so far-sighted, expansive and thoughtful, if slightly terrifying, on where AI could go, can basically play in this sort of dystopia about Europe and say things which are not true.
turns.zh: 欧洲并不是他描绘的那个地狱。我对此有些激动，可能比我应该的还要激动，因为在我看来，这不仅是错误的，而且是不负责任的，并且正在带来非常严重的后果。我觉得很不幸的是，一个在 AI 发展上如此有远见、开阔且深思熟虑的人，尽管有点令人畏惧，却会在欧洲问题上玩这种反乌托邦的叙事，说一些不真实的话。

turns.en: You've known Elon for a long time. I've known Elon for a long time, and I think we both agree that in many ways he's very brilliant and very thoughtful. So my question to you: to the degree that you disagree with his assessment, where do you think that assessment comes from? Why do you think he thinks that?
turns.zh: 你认识 Elon 很久了。我也认识 Elon 很久，我想我们都同意他在很多方面非常聪明、很有思想。所以我想问你：既然你不同意他的判断，你觉得他的这种判断来自哪里？你认为他为什么这么想？

turns.en: I think he has a very firmly held belief that if you have a large-scale migration of people from cultures that don't integrate, it will have problematic consequences for a society. To some degree one can agree with bits of that. Uncontrolled migration is societally untenable. But that's not what's happening in Europe. My issue with him is his, I think, erroneous and caricatured description of what's actually going on in Europe. The fact that he hasn't been here and that he is reposting and propagating things that are just not true kind of reinforces this negative spiral, particularly on X, which paints a picture of the continent that isn't accurate and which is in turn feeding the whole MAGA view that there's civilizational erasure in Europe. We're all, it's a dying continent in catastrophic shape. Of course, there are problems and I'm the first person to admit that. There are free speech issues in this country, there are problem areas, there are definitely some problems with migration. But it is not what he paints it to be, nor, frankly, is he being disingenuous when he says that all he is in favor of is secure borders, limited spending and safe cities, because on two out of three of those, Europe does better than the US.
turns.zh: 我认为他有一个非常坚定的信念：如果你接纳大量来自不融合文化的移民，那会给社会带来问题。在某种程度上，这种说法有一定的道理。不受控制的移民在社会上确实难以为继。但那不是欧洲正在发生的事。我不同意的是他对欧洲实际情况的错误和夸张描述。他本人没来过这里，却转发和传播不实的东西，这加剧了这种负面螺旋，尤其是在 X 上，这给欧洲描绘了一幅不准确的图景，反过来又助长了 MAGA 那种欧洲正在遭遇文明抹除的看法。好像我们是一个即将消亡、状况灾难性的大陆。当然，确实有问题，我是第一个承认的。这个国家有言论自由问题，有问题区域，移民也肯定有一些问题。但情况并非他所描绘的那样，而且坦率地说，当他说他只支持安全边界、有限支出和城市安全时，他有点不老实，因为这三项里有两项欧洲做得比美国好。

transcript.secZh: 马斯克反乌托邦欧洲观

turns.en: You also got into a bit of a fiery exchange with him over DOGE and USAID.
turns.zh: 你也在 DOGE 和 USAID 的问题上和他有过一次激烈的交锋。

turns.en: We did. He got fiery. I was just really asking him. He mentioned his view that USAID was just a political organization. And he said there had been zero deaths as a result of shutting down USAID. I simply pushed back and said, you know, it happened overnight. USAID was a very big provider of healthcare funding in Africa. I find it very hard to believe that there were no deaths and no suffering. And he just said zero. Zero deaths. Again, I think you can agree that USAID needed reform or perhaps even shutting down, but the way it was done clearly, to my mind and I think indisputably, has led to unnecessary suffering.
turns.zh: 是的。他变得很激动，我只是在问他问题。他提到他认为 USAID 只是一个政治组织。他还说关闭 USAID 没有导致任何死亡。我只是反驳说，这件事发生在一夜之间，USAID 在非洲是非常大的医疗资金提供者。我非常难以相信没有死亡和痛苦。他就像你听到的那样，只说零，零死亡。再次，我认为你可以同意 USAID 需要改革甚至可能需要关闭，但它的实施方式，在我看来，显然且无可争议地导致了不必要的痛苦。

turns.en: When you think about SpaceX, the IPO just happening and Tesla, we keep having a sort of a parlor game about whether he ultimately buys that business. What do you think? Does it all become one?
turns.zh: 当你想到 SpaceX 刚上市，还有特斯拉，我们一直在玩一个客厅游戏——他最终会不会买下那家公司。你怎么看？它们会合并为一体吗？

turns.en: He didn't talk about it explicitly, but my strong sense from the way he described his vision was that it was one set of businesses. When he talked about the reason for his control, and this was really interesting because I said, you have over 80% of voting shares, you essentially can't be removed even if you go crazy. He talked about why he needed this control, and he spoke about it in a 5 to 10 year time horizon. He said, 'I need it for the next 5 to 10 years because we have to extend consciousness to the universe.' And he described all the elements which included elements from SpaceX and from Tesla.
turns.zh: 他没有明确说明，但根据他描述愿景的方式，我强烈感觉那些是一组业务。当他谈到他需要控制权的原因时，这非常有意思，因为我说，你拥有超过 80% 的有投票权股份，你就算发疯也不会被踢走。他谈到为什么需要这种控制权，并且提到 5 到 10 年的时间维度。他说：“我需要在未来 5 到 10 年拥有它，因为我们必须将意识扩展到宇宙。”他描述了所有要素，其中包括 SpaceX 和特斯拉的要素。

transcript.sec: End of the interview on amicable terms

turns.en: You could tell I think that he has a lot of respect for you, but you guys had a lot of debate. I want to know how it ended.
turns.zh: 你能看出他对你非常尊重，但你们有很多辩论。我想知道那是怎么结束的。

turns.en: I think you saw it at the end. It ended perfectly amicably. He said, 'At least I'm not boring.' And then we carried on talking for another 15 minutes while he had his pictures taken. Look, I think he's an extraordinary individual. I am not a Musk hater. I think he's an extraordinary individual who has done probably more than any other person to build the future. So, I love talking to him. It was an incredible privilege to have what, 90 minutes talking to him. And we ended perfectly amicably. I hope he'll talk to me again. We'll see. It was really interesting, but it was important to push back on these areas where I think it deserves being pushed back on, because I just think it's not right what he's saying.
turns.zh: 我想你在最后也看到了。我们非常友好地结束了交谈。他说，“至少我不无聊。”然后我们在他拍照时又继续聊了大概 15 分钟。我想，他是个非凡的人。我不是 Musk 憎恨者。我认为他是一个非凡的人，很可能比任何其他人对构建未来做的贡献都多。所以，我喜欢和他交谈。能和他谈上 90 分钟，是一种难以置信的荣幸。我们非常友好地结束了。我希望他会再次跟我聊。拭目以待。这非常有意思，但在这些领域上反驳他很重要，我认为这值得反驳，因为我觉得他说的不对。

transcript.sec: Lina Khan's new role in New York

turns.en: Wall Street facing a major shakeup of New York City's situation. This after Mayor Adams named former FTC Chair Lina Khan as economic development chair. Joining us to discuss what this means for New York City's business climate, Steven Fullop, who's president and CEO of Partnership for New York City. We said earlier that this might have come as a surprise. I don't know if it should have come as a surprise because she was involved in the transition. What do you think?
turns.zh: 华尔街正面临纽约市局势的重大变化。此前市长 Adams 任命前 FTC 主席 Lina Khan 为经济发展主席。加入我们讨论这对纽约市商业环境意味着什么的是 Partnership for New York City 的总裁兼 CEO Steven Fullop。我们之前说这可能是一个意外。我不知道是否应该感到意外，因为她参与了过渡工作。你怎么看？

turns.en: I mean, I think it's a fair point. I know we always spoke about the positive relationship and the closeness between Lina Khan and Mayor Adams. Look, we have concerns and trepidations that she's in such a prominent role. And the question is going to be really how much does he lean on her in this new EDC position?
turns.zh: 我是说，我认为这一点说得很对。我知道我们一直在谈论 Lina Khan 和 Adams 市长之间的积极关系和密切程度。听着，我们对她在如此显要的职位上有所担忧和不安。问题在于，他在这个新的 EDC 职位上到底会多大程度地依赖她。

transcript.sec: concerns about mayoral appointments and pro-business stance

turns.en: What kind of changes or things are you already hearing that could be good or bad for business?
turns.zh: 你已经听到哪些变化或动向，可能对商业有利或不利？

turns.en: Look, when he came in, he kind of redefined the position of economic development around economic justice. We had a lot of questions around what economic justice means when you think about incentivizing businesses to grow here in New York City. We had a lot of hope that we would get somebody in the EDC leadership that we were familiar with. We got it in one of the two positions he appointed — we felt great about Tony being in the president position. But there's only one boss, Andrew, as you know, and the question is going to be who does the mayor lean on? We know that he has a history with Lina Khan that is very close.
turns.zh: 你看，他上任时，基本上是用经济正义重新定义了经济发展这个岗位。我们对“经济正义”有很多疑问，特别是当你考虑激励企业在纽约市发展的时候。我们曾非常希望 EDC 领导层里能有我们熟悉的人，他任命了两个职位，其中一个我们很满意——Tony 担任总裁让我们感觉很好。但是你知道，老板只有一个，Andrew，问题在于市长会依靠谁。我们知道他跟 Lina Khan 交情很深。

turns.en: She's known at the FTC, Steven, as being sort of adversarial to big business. What are the major concerns you have that in this new role she can actually make life more difficult for businesses operating in the city?
turns.zh: 她在 FTC 时，大家都知道她有点跟大企业对着干，Steven。你主要担心的是什么？她在这个新位置上真的会让在纽约做生意的企业日子更难过吗？

turns.en: Look, this is a major shift if you pursue a regulatory environment with the EDC that is rooted in a history of incentivizing business and growth here. There are a lot of questions around the DSA and a Democratic Socialist mayor. You've seen some companies say over the last couple months that they're going to grow elsewhere — Texas, Florida. Language matters from the executive. So when you put people in prominent positions that aren't necessarily pro-business, it sends a message to the business community that is mixed at best. That's kind of where we are.
turns.zh: 你看，如果 EDC 真的要推行一套监管环境，而它历史上一直是激励商业和发展，那就彻底转向了。DSA 和一个民主社会主义市长，这里有很多疑问。过去几个月，已经有公司说要去别处发展——得克萨斯、佛罗里达。执政者说的话很重要。所以当你不把亲商的人放在显要位置上，就是在向商界释放一个顶多算混杂的信号。我们差不多就是这个状况。

transcript.secZh: 市长任命与亲商立场担忧

transcript.sec: the incremental impact on business decisions

turns.en: Do you think this makes a difference? If a business were making a decision today about whether to expand, relocate, or establish a presence in New York City, would this appointment be bad — a negative input into that decision-making process?
turns.zh: 你觉得这会有影响吗？如果一家企业今天在决定要不要扩张、搬迁或在纽约设点，这个任命会是坏事吗——会成为决策过程中的一个负面因素？

turns.en: Look, I think everything is incremental — positive and negative. You see people making decisions and they're hedging. You've had some positive indicators: job growth in New York City over the last couple months has been great. New York City is a resilient place. But at the same time you see a long-term trend of wealthy people leaving, which independent entities are citing. And you have companies like Apollo, Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, Citadel talking about scaling up elsewhere. So it's a mixed bag, and all of these things are additive in a direction of positive or negative. I would put her being there on the negative side. But is it going to be the overwhelming decision-making factor? Probably not, but it will move people closer in that direction for sure.
turns.zh: 我觉得一切都是渐进的——正面和负面都是。人们在决策时会两边下注。有一些积极信号：过去几个月纽约市就业增长很不错，纽约是个很有韧性的地方。但同时你也看到富人外流的长期趋势，独立机构也这么指出。还有像 Apollo、高盛、摩根大通、Citadel 这些公司都在谈论去其他地方扩张。所以局面很复杂，所有这些因素都在往正面或负面方向叠加。我会把她的到来归为负面。但这会成为压倒性的决策因素吗？大概不会，但肯定会把人往那个方向推。

transcript.secZh: 对商业决策的渐进影响

transcript.sec: relationship with city hall and tangible cooperation

turns.en: What do you think the relationship is right now? When you go to City Hall, is the relationship better, worse, frosty? Can you point to things they're doing that you like? I just want to understand what it's actually like in the room.
turns.zh: 你觉得现在关系怎么样？你去市政厅的时候，关系是好了、坏了，还是冷淡了？有没有什么他们做的事是你喜欢的？我只是想了解真实情况如何。

turns.en: Yeah, look, a couple days ago the mayor changed the regulatory environment around small businesses, making it easier for them to open. We were a cheerleader and continue to be a cheerleader for that. We've had several one-on-one conversations, and he's been to the partnership before, and he's a talented communicator — no question about that. He would point to things like American Express opening or breaking ground on a new headquarters here as a positive indicator, and we would say that's great news. The city is very resilient. American Express has been here over a century. However, those things are performative when you go to ribbon cuttings and groundbreakings. We're looking for places to overlap — whether it's on child care, AI and job displacement, housing growth — that are concrete and encouraging the private sector to grow. We just haven't gotten there yet.
turns.zh: 嗯，几天前市长改变了小企业的监管环境，让开业更容易，我们当时就是拉拉队，现在也还是。我们有过几次一对一谈话，他以前也来过我们商会，他确实是个很有天赋的沟通者，这点毫无疑问。他会举美国运通在纽约开设或动工新总部这类事作为积极信号，我们也会说这是好消息。这座城市很有韧性，美国运通在这里已经超过一个世纪了。但是，当你去参加剪彩和动工仪式时，这些事总有些表演成分。我们在找真正的交集——不管是儿童照护、AI 与工作岗位流失、住房增长——这些能实实在在鼓励私营部门发展的领域。我们还没走到那一步。

transcript.secZh: 与市政厅的关系及实际合作

transcript.sec: the pied-à-terre tax tweet and campaign rhetoric

turns.en: I was surprised — the mayor put out a tweet yesterday. I don't know if you saw it. It said, 'If you have a second home in New York City worth more than $5 million, check your mailbox when you're back in the five boroughs because you've got mail. Today we sent notification letters to property owners letting them know that our new pied-à-terre tax is coming soon.' The reason I mention this is the tone. Especially after the back-and-forth with Ken Griffin, maybe I shouldn't be surprised. But I thought he had taken a more conciliatory tone — like, we want all New Yorkers, if they want to be in New York and have a pied-à-terre, we love for you to have one, pay the tax, that's great. And if you want to live here, that's great. But this seemed to indicate he wasn't so happy that you were even here if you had a pied-à-terre.
turns.zh: 我很惊讶——市长昨天发了条推文。不知道你看到没。上面说：“如果你在纽约市有一套价值超过 500 万美元的第二套房，等你回到五区后检查一下信箱，因为有你的邮件。今天我们向业主寄出了通知信，告知新的非自住房税很快就要开征。” 我提这个是因为它的语气。特别是在跟 Ken Griffin 来了一个回合之后，也许我不该惊讶。但我原以为他的调子已经放缓了——像是：我们欢迎所有纽约人，如果你想待在纽约、有套第二套房，我们很高兴你有，请你交税，很棒；想住在这里，也很棒。但这条推文似乎在说，你有第二套房，他就不太高兴你在这儿。

turns.en: Yeah, look, the tax-the-rich conversation is red meat to his base. They had huge wins — the DSA and the far left — a couple weeks ago in the primaries here, and that was largely driven by the mayor's support. Over the last week or so, you saw the rhetoric around taxing the rich increase. You saw the rhetoric around Israel and Netanyahu increase, despite the fact that the mayor has no input over international or federal issues. So, those are campaign language, and we would hope that the priority remains keeping the city safe, paving streets, and encouraging economic development.
turns.zh: 嗯，对富人征税这个话题是他的基本盘最爱吃的红肉。几周前，DSA 和极左在本地初选中大胜，很大程度上是靠市长的支持推动的。过去一周左右，你看到向富人征税的调门升高了，关于以色列和内塔尼亚胡的调门也升高了，尽管市长对国际或联邦事务根本没有发言权。这些是竞选语言，我们希望重点仍然放在城市安全、铺路和鼓励经济发展上。

transcript.secZh: 小户型房产税推文与竞选言论

transcript.sec: the netanyahu comments and shifting overton window

turns.en: That's an interesting question. Let me ask you on the Netanyahu piece. As you watched that play out, and you're right, that's red meat for his base. But it also riles up the rest of the city. Somebody compared him to our president the other day and said, because I was making the argument he can't do this — this is before he came out and said he couldn't do it — and they said, well, he's going to say things he can't do just the way the president sometimes says things he's not going to do or can't do, and that this is just the new politics.
turns.zh: 这是个有意思的问题。我想问问关于内塔尼亚胡这一节。你看到这整件事的演变，你说得对，这是他基本盘的红肉。但同时也激怒了城市里的其他人。前几天有人把他比作我们的总统，说——因为我当时在争辩他不能这么做，那是在他公开说不能做之前——他们说，嗯，他会说些做不到的事，就像总统有时也会说些他不会做或者做不到的事，这就是新政治。

turns.en: Well, I don't necessarily agree, I don't agree with that Andrew. I think that the president when he says something—
turns.zh: 这个我不一定同意，我不同意，Andrew。我觉得总统说某些话的时候——

turns.en: I'm not defending it. I'm just suggesting this has become — maybe the Overton window has now shifted for everybody.
turns.zh: 我不是在替它辩护，我只是说这已经变得——也许奥弗顿窗口现在已经对所有人都移动了。

turns.en: Look, I think that there is an anti-Semitic component of the extreme left and extreme right for that matter.
turns.zh: 你看，我认为极左和极右就此而言都有反犹的成分。

transcript.secZh: 内塔尼亚胡评论与Overton窗口移动
